subject: Bootstrapping error message for IID individuals

messages.author: 1fda8c440cc6517f
messages.subject: Bootstrapping error message for IID individuals
parts:
Hi Dr. Fleming,

First, I want to say how grateful I am that you are so responsive to messages in this group, as I have been using many of the conversations to aid me in the workflow of the project I'm currently working on. I have been utilizing the CTMM package for this project, and I had a question about a certain error I've come across and cannot resolve. For our project, we are assessing potential home range shifts of Wood Thrush individuals using relocation data collected via VHF radio tracking. Since much of the data is so coarse as to have little to no autocorrelation between points (the home range crossing time of a forest bird like this is way smaller than our minimum sampling rate of six hours), most of the individuals' data is IID. However, the following error arises when I try to bootstrap the data from these IID individuals whose range is also isotropic using ctmm.boot:

Error in dim(ADD) <- c(length(NAMES), cores) :

  dims [product 0] do not match the length of object [2]

AND, if I catch the error and print the message:

<simpleError in dim(ADD) <- c(length(NAMES), cores): dims [product 0] do not match the length of object [2]>

Here is basically how I run the code to produce the error (bird_data is a single telemetry object):

GUESS <- ctmm.guess(bird_data,  interactive = FALSE)

FITS <- ctmm.select(bird_data, GUESS, trace = 3, verbose = TRUE, cores = 2)

BOOT <- ctmm.boot(bird_data, FITS[[1]], AICc = TRUE, iterate = TRUE, trace = TRUE, cores = 2)

This error doesn't occur when the data is IID anisotropic, nor when the best fit model is anything else. I'm just a relative beginner when it comes to programming and modeling, but I tried to debug a tiny bit and it seems that something might happen to the model when it is passed to ctmm.reduce that affects its COV attribute in a way that breaks the ctmm.boot function. Or it is certainly possible I am running the code incorrectly in the first place, either from a conceptual perspective or a coding one.

Also, here is a preliminary composite figure showing the info from one such bird if it would help. The home range estimate is from a non-bootstrapped model, Please forgive the slight formatting errors:


Do you have any thoughts on this error or a possible solution to get around it?


Thanks,

Charlie Dees

messages.subject: Re: Bootstrapping error message for IID individuals
parts:
Hi Charlie,

Please send me a minimal working example, so that I can fix the issue.

I will also make sure that I have ctmm.boot() coded correctly for IID processes - it shouldn't be doing anything without an error model, because REML is already MVU in that case.

Best,
Chris

Best,
